title: Seve Ballesteros's birth chart
metaDescription: Seve Ballesteros's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.3° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 19.3° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 19.3° of Aries is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Taurus (7.4°), Venus in Aries (18.0°), Mars in Gemini (14.2°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction declared rather than implied, effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Saturn — a opposition holding at 0.1°. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Uranus square Neptune at 1.3°, and the Sun conjunction Venus at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Neptune while both square Uranus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. The Sun in Aries at 19.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Aries at 18.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Virgo at 24.1° is in detriment. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 6 fire, 2 earth, 1 air, 1 water by element and 5 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by mode. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.4° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 10.5°.
